note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in WY.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Chief Joseph Scenic Highway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway (designated 1988 as the Chief Joseph Scenic Highway)
byways.where: WYO 296, 47 mi from WYO 120 north of Cody to US 212 (Beartooth Highway), Park County

facts.fact: In 1988 the Wyoming State Highway Commission designated the 47-mile WYO 296 in Park County as the Chief Joseph Scenic Highway, the state's first such designation.
The 47 paved miles run from the WYO 120 junction 17 miles north of Cody, through the Absaroka Mountains of the Shoshone National Forest to the Clarks Fork valley and US 212.
The road is named for Chief Joseph of the Nez Perce, who in 1877 led his people east through Yellowstone and north up the Clarks Fork while fleeing the U.S. Army.
Sunlight Basin, below the west side of Dead Indian Pass, is grizzly country, and bears are occasionally seen near the highway in spring.

byways.review: The state program's first road. The state's own 2009 list still uses the name Chief Joseph Scenic Highway. Travel Wyoming calls it Chief Joseph Scenic Byway.

byways.name: Beartooth Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also All-American Road and National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 212 from Red Lodge, Montana, to the Northeast Entrance of Yellowstone; Park County, WY

facts.fact: US 212 is the highest paved primary road in Wyoming, cresting at 10,947-foot Beartooth Pass, and is open to highway travel only from late May to mid-October.
Snowbanks often remain near Beartooth Pass until August, and some drifts last all summer.
Opened in 1936, the road roughly follows the Sheridan Trail laid out in 1882, and it is the only All-American Road in Wyoming.

byways.review: Wyoming lists it as Beartooth Scenic Byway; the catalog uses Beartooth Highway. Only part of the road lies in Wyoming.

byways.name: Buffalo Bill Cody Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 14/16/20, 27 mi from the Shoshone National Forest boundary west of Cody to Yellowstone's East Entrance

facts.fact: The 27 paved miles follow the North Fork of the Shoshone River through the Wapiti Valley from the forest boundary about 25 miles west of Cody to Yellowstone's East Entrance.
Pahaska Teepee along the route was Buffalo Bill's original hunting lodge.
The byway is open year round, but Yellowstone's East Entrance closes the first Monday of November.

byways.review: WYDOT's brochure groups it with the Beartooth and Chief Joseph as the Buffalo Bill - Yellowstone Country byways.

byways.name: Big Horn Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 14 between Dayton and Shell across the Bighorn National Forest; Sheridan and Big Horn counties

facts.fact: The Wyoming Transportation Commission adopted 47 miles of US 14 between Dayton and Shell as the Big Horn Scenic Byway.
Granite Pass at 9,033 feet is the high point of the route, which switchbacks through a canyon on the west side and descends more gradually on the east.
Shell Falls on the western end drops 120 feet and has nature trails and interpretive signs.

byways.review: Spelled Big Horn by WYDOT and Bighorn by the Forest Service and Travel Wyoming. Travel Wyoming gives 58 miles, the 2009 state list 47.

byways.name: Medicine Wheel Passage
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 14A, 27 mi west from Burgess Junction to the Bighorn National Forest boundary toward Lovell

facts.fact: The byway covers 27 miles of US 14A from Burgess Junction to the western edge of the Bighorn National Forest, with a maximum 10-percent grade, and is closed by snow in winter and early spring.
The Medicine Wheel on the slopes of Medicine Mountain is a circle of limestone boulders about 80 feet across with 28 rock spokes.
A viewpoint at 9,430 feet looks southwest into the Big Horn Basin.

byways.name: Cloud Peak Skyway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 16, 47 mi between Buffalo and Ten Sleep across the Bighorn National Forest

facts.fact: The 47-mile byway on US 16 crests at 9,666-foot Powder River Pass and gives the only view from the route of Cloud Peak, at 13,167 feet the highest in the Big Horn Mountains.
The rock walls of Ten Sleep Canyon line the west entrance, and Meadowlark Lake has a boat ramp along the way.

byways.name: Wyoming Centennial Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 26/287 and US 26/89/191, 163 mi from Dubois over Togwotee Pass via Moran Junction, Jackson and Hoback Junction to Pinedale; Fremont, Teton and Sublette counties

facts.fact: The 163-mile horseshoe of US 26/287 and US 26/89/191 crosses the Continental Divide at 9,658-foot Togwotee Pass.
Between Jackson and Moran Junction the byway passes through Grand Teton National Park, and near Pinedale is the Museum of the Mountain Man.
The byway spans two national forests, a national park and three counties, linking Dubois, Jackson and Pinedale.

byways.name: Snowy Range Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway; also National Forest Scenic Byway
byways.where: WYO 130, 29 mi of the Medicine Bow National Forest section between Centennial and Saratoga; Albany and Carbon counties

facts.fact: The route rises from 8,000 feet to 10,847 feet, and at Snowy Range Pass Medicine Bow Peak towers to 12,013 feet. Near the summit grow wind-shaped krummholz trees.
The byway is normally open from Memorial Day through October; the Mirror Lake Picnic Ground has a fishing platform and a lakeshore path.
WYO 130 was the second National Forest Scenic Byway in the United States.

byways.review: The 2009 state list gives 29 miles; the 2004 WYDOT brochure says 27.

byways.name: Mirror Lake Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway (also a Utah Scenic Byway)
byways.where: WYO 150, about 20-23 mi from Evanston south to the Utah line; continues as Utah 150 to Kamas

facts.fact: The byway is 80 miles in all between Evanston and Kamas, Utah: 23 miles of WYO 150 and 57 miles of Utah 150.

Leaving Evanston the route crosses sagebrush flats and aspen and conifer forest, with a panoramic view of the Uinta Mountains, the only major range in the contiguous United States with an east-west axis.

byways.review: Only the Wyoming section belongs here; the Utah part is in the Utah chapter.

byways.name: Flaming Gorge - Green River Basin Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway
byways.where: WYO 530 south from Green River to the Utah line and US 191 north to Rock Springs, looping around Flaming Gorge Reservoir; Sweetwater County

facts.fact: The byway begins at Green River and runs south on WYO 530 to the Utah border and north along US 191 to Rock Springs, about 100 miles in total.
John Wesley Powell set off down the Green River on May 24, 1869, from Expedition Island in the town of Green River.
Flaming Gorge Reservoir formed behind a dam at Red Canyon in Utah completed in 1964.

byways.review: Length given as 100 miles by WYDOT (2009) and 160 miles by tourism sources, which probably count the Utah connector around the reservoir.

byways.name: Bridger Valley Historic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway (historic byway)
byways.where: I-80 Business Loop between I-80 exits 34 and 48 through Lyman, Urie and Fort Bridger, with spurs to Mountain View and Carter; Uinta County

facts.fact: The byway is 13 miles of the I-80 Business Loop through Lyman, Urie and Fort Bridger, with a spur south to Mountain View and a 7-mile spur north to the old railroad town of Carter.

The loop runs from I-80 Exit 34 to Exit 48, and Fort Bridger has a museum and a replica of Jim Bridger's original 1843 trading post, next to the restored Orange and Black Tourist Court from early Lincoln Highway travel.

byways.review: No dedicated official page found; Travel Wyoming has no listing for it.

byways.name: Wind River Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 20/WYO 789, 32-34 mi from Shoshoni (MP 100) through Wind River Canyon to just north of Thermopolis (MP 134); Fremont and Hot Springs counties

facts.fact: The byway runs north from Shoshoni at milepost 100 through Wind River Canyon and the Wind River Indian Reservation to just north of Thermopolis at milepost 134.
The canyon walls rise 2,500 feet and expose Precambrian rock; interpretive signs identify each layer. At the Wedding of the Waters the Wind River becomes the Bighorn River.
The Wind River Indian Reservation is home to the Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho.

byways.review: Part of the route crosses the Wind River Indian Reservation of the Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho.

byways.name: Oregon Trail Historic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway (historic byway)
byways.where: US 26, 57 mi from the Nebraska line through Torrington, Lingle, Fort Laramie and Guernsey to I-25 at Dwyer Junction; Goshen and Platte counties

facts.fact: The byway follows US 26 from the Nebraska line through Torrington, Lingle, Fort Laramie and Guernsey to I-25 at Dwyer Junction, 57 miles.

Fort Laramie began in 1834 as a fur-trade post and was abandoned in 1890; Register Cliff near Guernsey is a sandstone cliff where emigrants left inscriptions, and the Oregon Trail ruts nearby are cut into solid rock.

byways.review: Not on the 2009 state list; designated later. Listed by Travel Wyoming and the Wyoming tourism byway brochure.

byways.name: Battle Pass Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway
byways.where: WYO 70 over the Sierra Madre between Encampment and Baggs; Carbon County

facts.fact: On November 15, 2012, the Wyoming highway commission designated WYO 70 as the Battle Pass Scenic Byway; the highway crosses Battle Pass at 9,955 feet in the Medicine Bow National Forest.

About 10 miles west of Encampment is the site of Battle, one of several Sierra Madre ghost towns, and two miles west of the Continental Divide a turnout overlooks Battle Lake and a monument to Thomas Edison, who vacationed there in 1878.
The pass is named for an 1841 fight between mountain men and Native Americans.

byways.review: Lengths disagree: 23 miles (tourism brochure), about 30 miles of forest section (Wikipedia), 57 miles of all of WYO 70 (Travel Wyoming). The GIS line covers all of WYO 70 from Baggs to Encampment, about 58 miles.

byways.name: Wyoming Black Hills Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway
byways.where: Wyoming Black Hills around Newcastle toward Sundance (US 85 and WYO 585 area); Weston and Crook counties. Exact route not confirmed from an official source

facts.fact: The 78-mile Wyoming Black Hills Scenic Byway lies at the western gateway to the Black Hills; nearby are the ghost towns of Cambria and Tubb Town and sites such as the Jenny Stockade and the Anna Miller Museum.
The pine-covered hills look dark from a distance, in contrast to the open grasslands around them.

byways.review: Length given as 78 miles (listing, brochure) and 46 miles (Travel Wyoming byways page). The GIS line measures about 106 miles and stops short of Sundance; check before drawing.

byways.name: Star Valley Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 89 (and US 26/89), 80 mi from the Idaho line (MP 54.9) over Salt River Pass through Afton and Alpine to the Lincoln-Teton county line; Lincoln County

facts.fact: An 80-mile stretch of US 89 in Lincoln County, from the Idaho line at milepost 54.9 up Salt Canyon to the 7,610-foot summit of Salt River Pass, then down Star Valley through Smoot, Afton, Grover, Thayne and Etna to Alpine.
From Alpine the byway follows US 26/89 east into the Snake River Canyon to the Lincoln-Teton county line about nine miles south of Hoback Junction.

byways.review: Called Wyoming's newest scenic byway by Travel Wyoming; designation date not found. No GIS line found in any layer.

byways.name: South Big Horn/Red Wall Scenic Backway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Backway; also BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: Natrona County roads 125, 109 and 105, a 102-mi horseshoe off US 20/26 between Casper and Waltman

facts.fact: The byway starts 13 miles northwest of Casper at US 20/26 and Natrona County Road 125, follows the 33-mile Stock Driveway to Buffalo Creek and the Red Wall, and returns on County Road 105 to US 20/26 at Waltman.
The 102-mile route is mostly gravel for high-clearance vehicles; ponderosa pines appear past Fifty-Mile Flat, and Hole-in-the-Wall lies not far north of the Red Wall.

byways.name: Red Gulch/Alkali Scenic Backway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Backway; also BLM National Back Country Byway
byways.where: 32 mi of graded county roads from US 14 four miles west of Shell south to WYO 31 near Hyattville; Big Horn County

facts.fact: The 32-mile route on gravel and dirt roads runs from US 14 four miles west of Shell to WYO 31 north of Hyattville, past hoodoos and the boundary of the Alkali Creek Wilderness Study Area.
The Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite, found in 1997 in Middle Jurassic rock, is the largest dinosaur track site in Wyoming.
The red hills along the road are the Chugwater formation, laid down about 230 million years ago.

byways.name: Seminoe to Alcova Scenic Backway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Backway; also BLM Back Country Byway
byways.where: Carbon County Road 351 and Natrona County Road 407, 64 mi from I-80 exit 219 at Sinclair to WYO 220 at Alcova

facts.fact: The 64-mile byway follows County Road 351 north from Sinclair (I-80 exit 219) into Natrona County as County Road 407 to Alcova, past Seminoe, Pathfinder and Alcova reservoirs and the Miracle Mile, a blue-ribbon trout fishery of the North Platte.
The stretch through the Seminoe Mountains to the Miracle Mile is very steep and not recommended for motor homes or trailers.

byways.name: Big Spring Scenic Backway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Backway
byways.where: WYO 233, Forest Road 10062 and WYO 232 between Kemmerer and Cokeville through the Bridger National Forest; Lincoln County

facts.fact: The 68-mile backway from Kemmerer to Cokeville crosses emigrant trails and enters the Tunp Range of the Bridger National Forest; high-clearance vehicles are recommended west of Kelley Guard Station.
Wagon ruts from the Oregon Trail era are still visible in places, and 4-wheel drive is highly recommended on the unimproved Forest Service road.
Abandoned homesteads such as the Old Settler Cabin are visible from the road.

byways.review: Spelled Big Springs in the 2009 state list.

byways.name: Muddy Creek Historic Backway
byways.designation: Wyoming Scenic Backway (historic backway)
byways.where: Gravel roads numbered 219, 217, 212, 202 and 173 from Fort Bridger to Piedmont and I-80 exit 24; Uinta County

facts.fact: About 25 miles of gravel road from Fort Bridger lead past Muddy Creek to the ghost town of Piedmont and its charcoal kilns, a state historic site.
Muddy Creek was used by Brigham Young's first group of Mormon pioneers in 1847 and later held an Overland Stage stop and Pony Express station.

byways.review: Travel Wyoming writes the route numbers as WY-219 and so on, but these are gravel roads; its Mirror Lake listing calls 173 a county road.

issues: WYDOT has no current list online. The 2009 program book lists 12 byways and 5 backways; Travel Wyoming now lists 21, adding Oregon Trail Historic Byway, Battle Pass, Wyoming Black Hills and Star Valley. Only Battle Pass has a sourced designation date (Nov 15, 2012, via Wikipedia citing a dead WYDOT news release).

Travel Wyoming calls the Flaming Gorge-Green River Basin byway an All-American Road; FHWA lists no such AAR in Wyoming, and the tourism brochure says the Beartooth is the state's only one. The tourism claim looks wrong. Its length is 100 mi (WYDOT 2009) vs 160 mi (tourism).
Battle Pass length disagrees across sources (23, about 30, 57 miles). Black Hills: 78 vs 46 miles, and no official source states the route. The GIS lines for both come from a non-agency layer.
Star Valley Scenic Byway has no line in any layer found; it would have to be drawn from US 89 MP 54.9 to the Lincoln-Teton county line on US 26/89.

The tourism brochure also lists Black Gold Byway, Gold Flakes to Yellowcake Historic Mine Trail and Black Diamond Trail as historic mine trails. These do not appear to be Transportation Commission designations and are left out.

Old fs.usda.gov byway URLs (recarea, detail) now redirect to generic forest pages. New pages exist only for Wyoming Centennial, Big Spring and the Medicine Wheel Passage region; Bighorn and Cloud Peak use the Bighorn NF scenic-drives page or Travel Wyoming.
Bridger Valley Historic Byway has no working official page; url is null.
The flaminggorgecountry.com, windriver.org and nsbfoundation.com byway pages return 403 to scripted requests (the NSBF brochure PDF was read through WebFetch).
